messages:
marta: Heads-up: the sample-app search flow is flaky during onboarding. It calls what the docs call `/v1/admin/models/search` with param `query`, but the Python SDK only exposes `list_models(name=...)` and treats the param as `name`. curl + Postman work with `query`.
jon: oh that explains a support ticket I saw earlier. Is the mismatch in param name causing 400s? any error traces?

marta: Yep. Server returns 400 when calling sdk wrapper like `client.list_models(name='invoice')` because server expects `query` and we send `name`. Error: `400 InvalidParameter: unknown parameter name`. Curl: `curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/models/search -d '{"query":"invoice"}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY'` returns hits.

kevin: Brutal. This seems like an RPC surface mismatch AND conceptual mismatch (search vs list). SDK should either map `name`->`query` or expose search explicitly. Also noticed the node SDK has a `searchModels({q: '...'})` helper. Parity bug for sure.

marta: Another subtlety: Node streaming from the search endpoint returns newline-delimited JSON chunks without an explicit event prefix; Python's streaming helper expects SSE-like `data:` lines and drops first chunk. So even when the params match, streaming results get truncated for py clients.

jon: So three problems: 1) param name drift (`name` vs `query`), 2) missing search API in py, 3) streaming format difference. All cause onboarding friction.

kevin: Quick mitigation ideas: (a) Add a tiny mapping layer in the py quickstart that POSTs to `/v1/admin/models/search` with requests when client.search(...) is missing. (b) Add a short compatibility shim in py SDK to accept `query`/`name` aliases. (c) Update docs to call out streaming chunk format and provide both patterns.

marta: Can we short-term add a snippet in quickstart README? Something like:
```
# fallback using requests
import os, requests
resp = requests.post(
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/models/search',
  json={'query': 'invoice'},
  headers={'Authorization': f"Bearer {os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']}"},
  stream=True
)
for line in resp.iter_lines(decode_unicode=True):
    if not line: continue
    print(line)
```
This will avoid the 400 and surface streaming chunks raw.

jon: Good. Long-term we should do: add `search_models(query=...)` to py, add input aliasing for backwards compatibility, and standardize streaming format across SDKs (or document both and provide helpers).

kevin: Also flagging retry semantics: the search endpoint is idempotent but returns 429 under heavy load; node SDK uses an exponential backoff + jitter for 429, python currently only retries on connection errors. That leads to failed onboarding jobs in CI where the node version silently recovers but python fails fast.

marta: Could we add a small retry decorator in quickstart snippet to help folks running the sample? Example: `tenacity.retry(wait=wait_exponential, stop=stop_after_attempt(5), retry=retry_if_exception_type(requests.exceptions.RequestException))` around the requests call.

jon: Please open an SDK parity GH issue listing: param mapping, new search surface, streaming format normalization, and 429 retry policy alignment. Tag devex + eng-runtime. Also add a tiny CI e2e in quickstart that POSTS to admin/search via REST so we detect drift quickly.

kevin: I'll draft the issue and add proposed code snippets and a unit test plan. Also suggest adding an integration test that asserts py and node streaming produce the same concatenated JSON list for the same query.

devex-bot: Created issue #789: "py-sdk parity: admin models search, param aliasing, streaming format, and retry alignment" labeled devex/priority-high. https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/789

marta: Thanks — i patched the quickstart with the requests fallback and added a note about retries + streaming. will follow up with the issue PR links. :thumbsup:
